content: When a customer explicitly asks to try a product, hand it over immediately—do not ask more questions.
Use the in-store environment for live demonstrations (tilt screen under light, play audio, show settings) to address concerns visually.
Always be prepared to close: know stock availability, pricing, and alternatives before the customer asks.
Avoid introducing uncertainty (e.g., 'not on sale in Italy') without offering a solution like a similar model or pre-order.
For family buyers, emphasize how the product benefits each family member (learning for kids, entertainment for all).

name: Immediate Hands-On Handover
condition: When a customer explicitly asks to try a product or shows strong interest in a feature.
example: Customer: 'Let me try the pen.' Salesperson: 'Here you go—write anything and feel the response.'

name: Live Environment Demonstration
condition: When the customer raises a concern that can be visually proven (glare, sound, speed).
example: Customer: 'Does the screen reduce glare?' Salesperson: 'Watch—I'll tilt it under the light. See? No mirror effect.'

name: Family Benefit Framing
condition: When the customer mentions family members or multiple use cases.
example: Customer: 'For the whole family.' Salesperson: 'This tablet works for Matteo's schoolwork, your Netflix nights, and even Sofia's drawing.'

objection: Is the MatePad Air available in Italy?
rebuttal_template: I understand your concern. While the MatePad Air isn't officially sold here, we have the [Model X] in stock right now with the same PaperMatte display and M-Pencil support. Let me show you—you can try it yourself at this table.

objection: Will the pen tip wear out quickly?
rebuttal_template: Great question. Let me show you the replacement tip pack we have right here—it costs only €[price] and lasts a full school year. You can even try writing on the screen now to feel the durability.

objection: Does the screen really reduce eye strain?
rebuttal_template: Absolutely. Let me open the Eye Care mode in Settings—you can see the SGS certification right here. And watch this: I'll hold the tablet under the bright store light—no glare, just clear content. You can try it yourself.
